extra_vocab.en: a person whose job is to check that things are safe or correct
extra_vocab.note: 指專門到現場檢查的人，如安全、衛生、建築檢查員。這句中的 inspector 到店裡評估損害，是多益常見的保險、品管、設施情境。

example.en: Two inspectors checked the warehouse before it reopened.
example.zh: 兩名檢查員在倉庫重新開放前做了檢查。

example.en: The safety inspector found a problem with the fire exit.
example.zh: 安全檢查員發現防火出口有問題。

example.en: A health inspector will visit the restaurant next week.
example.zh: 衛生檢查員下週會到這家餐廳視察。

example.en: The building inspector approved the plans on Monday.
example.zh: 建築檢查員在週一核准了設計圖。

examples.en: An inspector will visit the store to assess the damage.
examples.zh: 檢查員會到店裡評估損害。

examples.en: Our quality inspector rejected the whole batch of products.
examples.zh: 我們的品管檢查員退回了整批產品。

confusable.diff: 拼法與字根相近，但 spectator 是看比賽或表演的「觀眾」，不負責檢查。

example.en: Spectators filled the stadium long before the game began.
example.zh: 比賽開始前很久，觀眾就坐滿了體育場。

confusable.diff: auditor 檢查的是帳目與財務紀錄；inspector 檢查的是現場、設備或產品。

example.en: The auditor reviewed last year's accounts and found no errors.
example.zh: 查帳員檢視了去年的帳目，沒有發現錯誤。

example.en: Please ask your supervisor to sign this form.
example.zh: 請請你的主管簽署這份表格。

example.en: The safety officer checks every machine each morning.
example.zh: 安全負責人每天早上檢查每一台機器。

derived.link: 詞幹 inspect，仔細檢查；加 -or 變成做這件事的人，像 actor、visitor。
inspect + -ion，把「檢查」變成名詞，像 action、decision。

extra_vocab.en: the amount of a product that people want to buy
extra_vocab.note: 這句中的 demand 是名詞，指市場對產品的「需求」，常和 supply（供給）、forecast（預測）一起出現。當動詞時是「強烈要求」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: demand 當名詞時常接 for：demand for + N（對…的需求），不接 of。

example.en: The company could not meet all the workers' demands.
example.zh: 公司無法滿足工人所有的要求。

example.en: The new law demands clear labels on every product.
example.zh: 新法規要求每項產品都要有清楚的標示。

example.en: The client demanded a quick answer to his complaint.
example.zh: 客戶要求對他的抱怨盡快給答覆。

example.en: The manager is demanding faster delivery from every supplier.
example.zh: 經理正要求每家供應商加快交貨。

example.en: She works for a very demanding boss at the bank.
example.zh: 她在銀行替一位要求很高的老闆工作。

example.en: Skilled engineers are in demand in this region.
example.zh: 這個地區很需要技術工程師。

example.en: There is strong demand for electric cars this year.
example.zh: 今年電動車的需求很強。

example.en: We hired extra workers to meet demand during the holidays.
example.zh: 我們僱用了額外人手來應付假期的需求。

example.en: Prices depend on supply and demand in the market.
example.zh: 價格取決於市場的供給與需求。

examples.en: Forecasting demand correctly helps the company avoid extra storage costs.
examples.zh: 正確預測需求能幫公司避免額外的倉儲成本。

examples.en: Customer demand dropped sharply after the price went up.
examples.zh: 價格調漲後，顧客需求大幅下降。

examples.en: Customers demand fast service and clear information.
examples.zh: 顧客要求快速的服務與清楚的資訊。

confusable.diff: 拼法與發音接近，但 command 是上對下的「命令」或「掌握」；demand 是強烈要求，不一定有上下關係。

example.en: The general manager gave a command to stop production at once.
example.zh: 總經理下令立刻停止生產。

similar.diff: request 較客氣；demand 語氣強硬，要求對方一定要做到。

example.en: Please send your request for a refund by email.
example.zh: 請用電子郵件寄出你的退款申請。

similar.diff: require 多指規定或需要；demand 是主動、強烈地要求。

example.en: This job requires two years of sales experience.
example.zh: 這份工作需要兩年的業務經驗。

example.en: The supply of parts is lower than last year.
example.zh: 零件的供應量比去年少。

example.en: There is a growing need for online training.
example.zh: 對線上訓練的需要越來越多。

example.en: Demand for our new phone is higher than expected.
example.zh: 我們新手機的需求比預期高。

example.en: The union demands better pay for night shifts.
example.zh: 工會要求夜班有更好的薪資。

senses.en: the amount of a product that people want to buy

example.en: Demand for office space has fallen since more people work from home.
example.zh: 自從更多人在家工作，辦公室空間的需求下降了。

senses.en: a strong request that must be met
senses.distinguish: 講的是人提出的要求，常用複數 demands；講商品用 demand for。

example.en: The workers made three demands at the meeting.
example.zh: 工人們在會議上提出了三項要求。

extra_vocab.en: people whose job is to study information and explain what it means
extra_vocab.note: 這句中的 Analysts 是複數主詞，指研究市場或數據並提出預測的分析師，多益常見於財經新聞與市場報告。

example.en: A financial analyst advised us to wait before buying more shares.
example.zh: 財務分析師建議我們先別再多買股票。

example.en: The market analyst expects prices to fall next month.
example.zh: 市場分析師預期下個月價格會下跌。

example.en: Our data analyst prepares a sales report every Monday.
example.zh: 我們的數據分析師每週一準備銷售報告。

examples.en: Analysts forecast that demand will stay strong this year.
examples.zh: 分析師預測今年需求將持續強勁。

examples.en: The analysts presented their findings to the board on Friday.
examples.zh: 分析師們在週五向董事會報告了他們的發現。

confusable.diff: 字根相同，但 analysis 是「分析」這件事；analyst 是做分析的人。

example.en: The analysis shows that sales are highest on weekends.
example.zh: 分析顯示週末的銷售最高。

confusable.diff: consultant 是給公司建議與解決方案的顧問；analyst 主要研究資料並說明結果。

example.en: We hired a consultant to improve our customer service.
example.zh: 我們聘請了顧問來改善客戶服務。

example.en: The economist expects slow growth next year.
example.zh: 這位經濟學家預期明年成長緩慢。

example.en: A researcher called to ask about our survey.
example.zh: 一位研究員打來詢問我們的問卷調查。

derived.link: analyst 的動詞；-ize 常把名詞變成動詞，像 organize、summarize。
analyze 的名詞，分析這件事，複數是 analyses。

extra_vocab.en: likely to be good or successful
extra_vocab.note: 這句中的 promising 是形容詞，形容銷售預測「看好」。多益常用來形容結果、人才或市場很有希望。

example.en: The supplier always keeps its promises about delivery dates.
example.zh: 這家供應商總是遵守交貨日期的承諾。

example.en: The manager promised to reply to every customer by Friday.
example.zh: 經理答應在週五前回覆每位客戶。

example.en: The new store had a promising start in its first month.
example.zh: 新店在第一個月有個不錯的開始。

example.en: She is the most promising candidate for the sales job.
example.zh: 她是業務職位最有潛力的人選。

example.en: The test gave promising results for the new product.
example.zh: 測試為新產品帶來了令人期待的結果。

example.en: We always keep our promise to deliver on time.
example.zh: 我們一向遵守準時送達的承諾。

examples.en: The sales forecast for next year looks very promising.
examples.zh: 明年的銷售預測看起來非常樂觀。

examples.en: He is a promising young engineer at our company.
examples.zh: 他是我們公司一位有前途的年輕工程師。

examples.en: Asia is a promising market for our new software.
examples.zh: 亞洲是我們新軟體很有希望的市場。

confusable.diff: 拼法與發音接近，但 promote 是「促銷、升遷」；promise 是「承諾」或「有前途」。

example.en: The company will promote Ms. Lin to sales director next month.
example.zh: 公司下個月會升林小姐為業務總監。

similar.diff: encouraging 強調讓人感到鼓舞、有信心；promising 強調未來有成功的可能。

example.en: The latest survey results are very encouraging for us.
example.zh: 最新的調查結果讓我們非常受鼓舞。

example.en: We met a potential buyer at the trade show.
example.zh: 我們在商展上遇到一位潛在買家。

example.en: The meeting ended with a promising offer from the buyer.
example.zh: 會議以買方一個很有希望的報價作結。

example.en: The supplier made a promise to deliver by Friday.
example.zh: 供應商承諾在週五前送達。

example.en: He promised to send the contract tomorrow morning.
example.zh: 他答應明天早上寄出合約。

senses.en: signs that someone or something will do well
senses.distinguish: 常用 show promise；與「承諾」可從上下文分辨。

example.en: The young designer shows great promise in her first year.
example.zh: 這位年輕設計師在第一年就展現出很大的潛力。

senses.en: to show that something good is likely
senses.distinguish: 主詞是事物，常接 to V。

example.en: The new plan promises to cut costs by ten percent.
example.zh: 新計畫有望把成本降低百分之十。

extra_vocab.en: a rise in the amount or number of something
extra_vocab.note: 這句中的 increase 是名詞（重音在前），指價格的「上漲」。動詞 increase 重音在後 /ɪnˈkriːs/，意思是「增加」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: increase 當名詞接 in（an increase in sales），表示幅度用 of 或 by（an increase of 5%）。

example.en: Several price increases made customers choose cheaper brands.
example.zh: 幾次漲價讓顧客選擇了較便宜的品牌。

example.en: Demand usually increases before the holiday season.
example.zh: 需求通常在假期旺季前增加。

example.en: Sales increased by five percent last quarter.
example.zh: 上一季的銷售成長了百分之五。

example.en: Costs are increasing faster than our income this year.
example.zh: 今年成本增加的速度比我們的收入快。

example.en: There was a small increase in office rent this year.
example.zh: 今年辦公室租金小幅上漲。

example.en: Profits will increase by ten percent next year.
example.zh: 明年利潤將增加百分之十。

example.en: The report shows a significant increase in customer complaints.
example.zh: 報告顯示客訴明顯增加。

examples.en: We had to revise the forecast after the price increase.
examples.zh: 漲價之後，我們必須修改預測。

examples.en: The company announced a salary increase for all staff.
examples.zh: 公司宣布全體員工加薪。

examples.en: An increase in orders pushed the factory to work overtime.
examples.zh: 訂單增加讓工廠必須加班。

confusable.diff: 字根相同的反義字，decrease 是「減少」；兩字重音規則相同（名詞重音在前，動詞在後）。

example.en: A decrease in costs helped the company make more profit.
example.zh: 成本減少幫公司賺了更多利潤。

confusable.diff: 意思接近，但 raise 一定要接受詞；increase 可及物也可不及物。
confusable.usage: raise 是及物動詞，後面一定要有受詞（raise prices）；increase 可以說 Prices increased，不能說 Prices raised。

example.en: The store will raise its prices at the end of the month.
example.zh: 這家店會在月底調漲價格。

similar.diff: grow 強調自然成長，多用於公司或業績。

example.en: Our online business grew quickly during the past year.
example.zh: 我們的網路事業在過去一年快速成長。

similar.diff: boost 是主動推升，語氣較強。

example.en: The ad campaign helped boost sales in the spring.
example.zh: 廣告活動幫助春季的銷售提升。

example.en: Oil prices rose again at the beginning of the week.
example.zh: 油價在本週初再度上漲。

example.en: The company reported strong growth in the last quarter.
example.zh: 公司公布上一季有強勁的成長。

derived.link: increasing（持續增加的）+ -ly 變副詞，像 quickly、slowly。

example.en: Customers complained about the sudden increase in delivery fees.
example.zh: 顧客抱怨運費突然上漲。

example.en: We plan to increase our online sales by twenty percent.
example.zh: 我們計畫把線上銷售提高百分之二十。

extra_vocab.en: a time when something changes from an old way to a new way
extra_vocab.note: 文章談到人要從 critical 思考轉到 strategic 思考，這個「轉換」就是 transition；transition period 指轉換的這段期間，商務上常指換系統、換主管、換制度的過渡階段。
extra_vocab.pattern: during the transition period + 子句／a + 數字 + -month transition period
extra_vocab.grammar_note: transition 後面常接 to（transition to N）；a six-month transition period 的 month 用單數，因為整個詞組當形容詞用。

examples.en: Staff can use both systems during the transition period.
examples.zh: 過渡期間，員工可以同時使用兩套系統。

examples.en: The old manager will stay for a one-month transition period.
examples.zh: 舊任經理會留任一個月的過渡期。

examples.en: A six-month transition period will follow the new tax rule.
examples.zh: 新稅法之後會有六個月的過渡期。

similar.diff: adjustment period 強調適應新環境；transition period 強調從舊到新的轉換階段。

example.en: New employees usually need an adjustment period of a few weeks.
example.zh: 新進員工通常需要幾週的適應期。

confusable.diff: trial period 是試用、試行期，目的是測試；transition period 是轉換期。

example.en: Customers can use the software during a thirty-day trial period.
example.zh: 客戶可以在三十天的試用期內使用這套軟體。

extra_vocab.en: a short comment that someone says or writes
extra_vocab.note: remark 是中性偏正式的「一句評論」，常用於會議與演講，如 opening remarks（開場致詞）。當動詞時是「說、評論」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: remark 當動詞時常接 that 子句或 on／about：He remarked on the weak sales.

example.en: In his closing remarks, the CEO thanked every employee.
example.zh: 在閉幕致詞中，執行長感謝每一位員工。

example.en: She remarks that the team works well together.
example.zh: 她說這個團隊合作得很好。

example.en: The manager remarked that sales had improved this month.
example.zh: 經理說這個月的銷售有進步。

example.en: Several guests were remarking on the beautiful venue.
example.zh: 好幾位賓客都在談論這個漂亮的場地。

example.en: The director gave the opening remarks at nine o'clock.
example.zh: 主任在九點時做開場致詞。

example.en: The host will give the closing remarks after lunch.
example.zh: 主持人會在午餐後做結語。

example.en: Please do not make remarks about your coworkers' work.
example.zh: 請不要評論你同事的工作。

example.en: Many visitors remarked on the quality of our service.
example.zh: 許多訪客都稱讚了我們的服務品質。

examples.en: Her remark about the budget changed the whole discussion.
examples.zh: 她對預算的一句話改變了整場討論。

examples.en: The CEO's remark about new markets surprised the audience.
examples.zh: 執行長對新市場的評論讓聽眾很驚訝。

examples.en: Customers often remark that our staff are friendly.
examples.zh: 顧客常說我們的員工很親切。

confusable.diff: 字根相同，但 remarkable 是形容詞「出色的、值得注意的」，不是名詞「評論」。
confusable.usage: remark 是名詞或動詞；remarkable 是形容詞，修飾名詞。

example.en: The team made remarkable progress during the first quarter.
example.zh: 團隊在第一季有了顯著的進步。

similar.diff: comment 指對某事的看法，可口頭也可書面；remark 較偏口頭說出的一句話。

example.en: Please leave a comment on the draft before Friday.
example.zh: 請在週五前在草稿上留下意見。

derived.link: remarkable 的 -le 改成 -ly，像 comfortably、reliably。

example.en: His remark about the schedule made everyone laugh.
example.zh: 他對行程表說的那句話讓大家都笑了。

example.en: The auditor remarked that the records were very clear.
example.zh: 查帳員表示紀錄非常清楚。

extra_vocab.en: to think again about something and decide what you think of it now
extra_vocab.note: re- 是「再一次」，assess 是「評估」。文章提到要 assess the current situation（評估現況），reassess 則是情況改變後再評估一次，多益常用於重新檢視計畫、風險與優先順序。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: reassess 是及物動詞，直接接受詞（reassess the plan），不加 about。

example.en: She reassesses the risks at the start of every quarter.
example.zh: 她在每一季開始時重新評估風險。

example.en: We reassessed our budget after the supplier raised its prices.
example.zh: 供應商漲價後，我們重新評估了預算。

example.en: The team is reassessing its priorities for next year.
example.zh: 團隊正在重新評估明年的優先事項。

example.en: We need to reassess the situation before we make a decision.
example.zh: 做決定之前，我們需要重新評估情況。

example.en: Please reassess your priorities if the deadline changes.
example.zh: 如果截止日改變，請重新評估你的優先順序。

example.en: The bank will reassess the risk of the new loan.
example.zh: 銀行會重新評估這筆新貸款的風險。

examples.en: After the delay, the manager decided to reassess the project plan.
examples.zh: 延誤之後，經理決定重新評估專案計畫。

examples.en: Companies should reassess their strategy when the market changes quickly.
examples.zh: 當市場變化很快時，公司應該重新評估策略。

confusable.diff: 拼法與發音相近，但 reassure 是「使放心」，受詞是人；reassess 是「重新評估」，受詞是事物。
confusable.usage: reassure 的受詞是人（reassure customers）；reassess 的受詞是計畫、風險等事物。

example.en: The manager tried to reassure customers about the delivery delay.
example.zh: 經理試著讓客戶對交貨延誤放心。

confusable.diff: access 是「存取、進入」，沒有「重新」的意思，只是拼法與發音和 assess 相近。

example.en: Only managers can access the sales data on this server.
example.zh: 只有經理可以存取這台伺服器上的銷售資料。

similar.diff: 意思幾乎相同，re-evaluate 稍微更正式。

example.en: We must re-evaluate the plan before spending more money.
example.zh: 在多花錢之前，我們必須重新評估這個計畫。

similar.diff: review 是重新檢視一遍，不一定要重新下判斷。

example.en: Please review the contract again before you sign it.
example.zh: 簽約前請再把合約檢視一遍。

derived.link: 去掉 re- 就是 assess；re- 是「再一次」，像 redo、review。
